section_1.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
section_1.content: Define the state of an object. In classical physics, a system is always in one definite state. Introduce the concept of a 'bit' (0 or 1) as a prerequisite to contrast with the quantum 'qubit'.
section_1.example: A light switch: It is either ON or OFF. There is no middle ground.

section_2.title: Visualizing Superposition: The Mathematical Foundation
section_2.content: Introduce Dirac notation (|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩). Use a Bloch Sphere animation to visually represent superposition, showing the state vector as a point on the surface of a sphere, rather than just at the poles.
section_2.example: A spinning coin on a table: While spinning, is it Heads or Tails? It is a blur of both states simultaneously until it stops.

section_3.title: The Wave-Particle Duality
section_3.content: Explain that particles behave like waves. Show a probability wave function (Ψ) graph where the peak represents the location of the highest probability. Explain that 'superposition' is the interference of these waves.
section_3.example: Musical chords: A single note is a distinct state, but a chord is a superposition of multiple notes sounding at once to create a new harmonic.

section_4.title: The Act of Measurement: Wave Function Collapse
section_4.content: Explain the transition from the probabilistic superposition to a deterministic state upon observation. Emphasize that the observer influences the system, forcing it to 'choose' a state based on probability coefficients (α² and β²).
section_4.example: Schrödinger’s Cat: A cat in a box is both 'dead' and 'alive' until we open the box to 'measure' (observe) its state.

section_5.title: Quantum Advantage: Why Superposition Matters
section_5.content: Synthesize the knowledge. Explain that while classical computers process bits sequentially, quantum computers use superposition to perform massive parallel computations, solving complex problems in seconds.
section_5.example: A maze runner: A classical mouse explores one path at a time. A quantum mouse exists in a superposition of all paths simultaneously, finding the exit instantly.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
